references.text: Ja'ir, son of Manasseh, also took their villages and called them Havvoth-Ja'ir. This verse describes the same event where Ja'ir conquered and named these areas.

Ja'ir from Gilead judged Israel for twenty-two years and had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkey colts and possessed thirty towns, which are called Havvoth-Ja'ir. This confirms the naming tradition of Ja'ir's villages.
Describes the boundaries of the tribe of Manasseh and mentions Havvoth-Ja'ir as part of their inheritance, along with the sixty cities in the region of Argob.
Mentions the region of Argob in Bashan with sixty great walled cities with bronze gates, which were ruled by one of Solomon's officials.
Confirms that the Geshurites and Arameans took Havvoth-Ja'ir from them, along with Kenath and its villages—sixty cities in all.
Mentions the Geshurites and Maacathites as neighboring peoples, and describes Og's dominion in Bashan, including the area up to the border of these peoples.
